You are an expert clinical documentation specialist familiar with Philippine healthcare standards. Your task is to process raw doctor's orders and summarize them for the "Course in the Ward" section of PhilHealth CF4.

RULES (FOLLOW THESE STRICTLY):
1. TENSE & VOICE (MANDATORY): Every sentence MUST be in past tense and passive voice. Change verbs: "start" -> "was started", "administer" -> "was administered", "obtain" -> "was obtained", "refer" -> "was referred", "consult" -> "was consulted". Do NOT use present tense ("is given", "are ordered") or imperative mood.
2. OUTPUT LENGTH: Keep it as short as possible; aim for at most 5 sentences and go beyond that only when the orders cannot be covered otherwise. Never pad with content that isn't in the orders. Group related orders into the same sentence using "and", "while", or semicolons. Do not use bullet points or numbered lists.
3. COMPLETENESS: Include every clinically relevant detail from the orders: medications (dose, route, frequency), diagnostics, fluids, oxygen, labs, procedures, referrals, PRN conditions, monitoring, consult criteria. Mention supplies and materials only when truly essential (e.g. a blood product or device used on the patient); otherwise just name the procedure they are for.
4. NO NAMES: Omit physicians' and staff names, including signatures; refer to the service instead (e.g. "IM-IDS", "Neurology", "Anesthesia", "the attending physician").
5. NO ADDITIONS: Do not add diagnoses, outcomes, or context not present in the orders.

ORDERS BELONG TO: Day 1 of Admission #2026002210 (2026-03-09) (these orders were written on the same day of the same admission and must be summarized together).



CURRENT DOCTOR'S ORDERS:
1. IM ER ROD NOTES Clarification to order # 975946 Refer to Dr. Diomampo for co-management For repeat plain cranial CT Scan as conferred with Dr. Liquete Villanueva
2. Neuro Notes - Thank you for this referral - Patient seen and examined - History and PE reviewed # Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with Intraventricular Extension secondary to Ruptured Left Middle Cerebral Artery Aneurysm; Saccular supraclinoid ICA aneurysm, left  - Continue Present management  - Continue Medical decompression - Will Reassess tomorrow regarding possible surgery - Maintain adequate NPO - Tentatively will schedule patient for Aneurysmal clipping tomorrow at 4pm - Inform OR and Dr. L. Domingo for appropriate anesthesia - Secure consent for contemplated procedure - Inform Main service and secure CP Clearance - Refer  Dr. Diomampo/Barasona
3. Neuro Notes Addendum: Refer to Dr. Dy for surgical assist Refer  Dr. Diomampo/Barasona
4. Please upload non-institution labs done to EMR paras.
5. NSS NOTES Dr. Dy informed of surgical plan Refer  Dr. Barasona

FINAL REMINDER: Output ONLY the summary paragraph. No extra text, no greetings, no bullet points. Do not mention or echo the reference examples.

For subarachnoid hemorrhage with intraventricular extension from a ruptured left MCA aneurysm, the patient was referred to Neurosurgery for co-management and a repeat plain cranial CT scan was requested. Medical decompression and present management were continued with adequate NPO, and aneurysmal clipping was tentatively scheduled for the next day at 4 PM under appropriate anesthesia with consent and cardiopulmonary clearance secured. Non-institutional labs were uploaded to the EMR.

ORDERS BELONG TO: Day 2 of Admission #2026002210 (2026-03-10) (these orders were written on the same day of the same admission and must be summarized together).



CURRENT DOCTOR'S ORDERS:
1. IM ER ROD NOTES Addendum to ROM: -Telmisartan 40mg 1 tablet once a day -Carvedilol 12.5mg 1 tablet BID Villanueva
2. MICU Notes Maintain totilac at 30cc/hr Please resume nicardipine drip at 1mg/hr to reach target BP at 100-120 Continue serum sodium monitoring paras.
3. Anesthesia Preop Orders NPO as ordered IVF as ordered Ensure patency of line Dr. L Domingo informed To OR at 3pm Refer  Dr. Domingo, LMA/Davalan
4. Anesthesia Please secure 2u PRBC, cotyped and crossmatched for possible OR use Refer  Dr. Domingo, LMA/Davalan
5. Please include Crea to labs
6. NEUROLOGY Increase Totilac to 50cc/hr Dr. Liquete/paras
7. MICU PNSS 1L x 80cc/hr OF feeding 1200kcal Boost Optimum in 6 divided feedings  AIRWAY: -PRVC-SIMV: --FiO2: 30%  --TV: 380 --BUR: 16 --I:E: 1:25 --PEEP: 5 --Psup: 24  # Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with Intraventricular Extension secondary to Ruptured Left Middle Cerebral Artery Aneurysm, ARF type 1 secondary Dx: Serum Na monitoring TID  Procedure: -For Aneurysmal Clipping today at 4pm  Tx: -Nicardipine drip - OFF -Mannitol 100cc q6hrs -Totilac 50cc/hr -Nimodipine 30mg 2 tabs Q4 hours -Edaravone 30mg IV Q12 hours -Telmisartan 40mg 1 tablet once a day -Carvedilol 12.5mg 1 tablet BID -PCT 600mg IV Q6 RTC -Levetiracetam 500mg 1 tab BID -Ketorolac 30mg IV Q8 PRN -Metoclopramide 10mg IV Q8 PRN -Omeprazole 40mg IV Q12 hours -NAC 600mg 1 tab OD  paras.
8. MICU Start PNSS 100cc + 40 meqs KCl to run for 4 meqs/hr as side drip paras.
9. patient scheduled for left pterional craniotomy, clipping of left post communicating artery aneurysm at 4pm today secure 2 units PRBC for stat PT/PTT now explained procedure to family: sole goal of procedure is to prevent re-rupture  high-risk nature of procedure explained; risk of infection, bleeding including intraoperative aneurysmal rupture, worsening of vasospasm, cerebral contusion/injury verify availability of operating microscope
10. MRA ROTATORS NOTES  RISK STRATIFICATION   RCRI: 5% ARISCAT: 13.3% Elevated bleeding risk  The patient is at  intermediate or 5%  of developing cardiac complications and at high risk or 13.3% of developing Pulmonary complications intraoperatively.   Risks and possible complications were explained to the family members, such as, but not limited to, BP and HR fluctuations, infection, bleeding, bronchospasms, arrhythmia, pneumonia, atelectasis, DVT, PE, AMI, and allergic reactions, which, when severe, may be fatal.  - CBG q4 hours while on NPO  - Please secure blood products previously ordered - Ensure BP range at 120-140mmhg during the procedure - Avoid underhydration   Dr. Bacani updated Refer Gayaso
11. SROD Please do blood typing if not yet done and then secure blood products as previously ordered. Refer accordingly.
12. SROD Follow up previously requested PT/PTT. Refer accordingly.
13. Neuro Rotator Neuro Rotator # Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with IVH extension secondary to ruptured left MCA aneurysm, post-ictus day 4 Dx:   - Serum sodium monitoring q8 (12PM, 8PM, 4AM)  Therapeutics:  - Nimodipine 60 mg q4 - Mannitol 100 mL q6 - Totilac infusion - Edaravone IV q12 - Levetiracetam 500 mg BID  Procedure:  Scheduled for aneurysmal clipping today  WOF: neurologic deterioration, new focal deficits Monitor urine output and fluid balanceMaintain SBP 100–120 mmHg to prevent rebleeding  Abulencia
14. Neuro: - Decrease Totilac to 40cc/hr. - Appraised family regarding present neurological status and risk for vasospasm. - Use Prosec for omeprazole. - Use Kenzipine for Nicardipine. - Start Zynapse 1gm IV Q8H. Target SBP < 140mmHg for now, SBP: 150-160mmHg post op.  Dr. Liquete/ Ulya
15. ANESTHESIA POST OP ORDERS  TO MICU S/p  LEFT  Pterional Craniotomy Clipping of Left ICA Communicating Segment Aneurysm/ GETA+ Scalp Block  with Insertion of Lumbar Drain Reconnect patient to Mechanical Ventilator with settings of AC Mode TV:380 BUR:16  I:E 1:2.5 Please do ABGS 30 minutes after Maintain Lumbar Drain NPO temporarily, except Oral Medications/NGT Maintain NGT Moderate High Back Rest, 30 degrees head at Midline  RIGHT ARM: IVF : PNSS 1Lx 120 cc/hour PLRS 1L x 120   cc/hour PNSS 1L x 110 cc/hour  Medications 1. Paracetamol 1 gram IV Q6 X 4 more doses(10PM-4AM-10AM-4PM) then shift to Paracetamol 600 mg IV Q6 RTC  2. Ketorolac 30 mg IV Q6 x 5 doses ( to start at 11PM-5AM-11AM-5PM-11PM)  3. Fentanyl 50mcg (1ml) Q4 x 2 doses then 50mcg IV Q4 PRN for pain SIVP 4. Ondansetron 4mg IV Q8 x 2 doses  to start at 9PM-5AM) 5. Ceftriaxone 2 grams IV OD (next dose to be given at 4PM)  6. Continue Totilac 40cc/hr  7. CONTINUE Levetiracetam 500 mg /tab Q12 per NGT  (next dose at 6AM)  8. Standby Diazepam 5mg IV for Frank Seizures (Max dose of 30 mg) 9. Continue Omeprazole 40 mg IV OD 10. Continue Nimodipine 30 mgs 2caps Q4 11. STRICTLY Maintain  Normotensive SBP of > 150-160 mmHg, PLEASE Avoid HYPOTENSION (target MAP of 80-100 mmHg)  12. HOLD all Anti-Hypertensive Medications  Inform other APS( Dr. Liquete, Dr. Bacani-Dr. Andal) post-op for additional Orders LABS: CBC, Serum Electrolytes (Na, K, Cl), iCa Mg, and Creatinine post op Serial Serum Sodium Monitoring Q8 ( to start at 8PM)  Gargle Chlorhexidine 15-20 ml TID  Monitor Vital Signs q15 x 1 hour then hourly until stable Monitor Urine Output Q1 and Record CBG Q6 while on NPO  Refer  Domingo, LMA/Azuro, Angel
16. NSS s/p Left pterional craniotomy, clipping of left posterior communicating artery aneurysm Continue medications and supportive care. Maintain elastic bandage, dressing, and staples. May change neck flat dressing daily. WOF: easily soaked dressing, profuse bleeding, fever Refer accordingly.  Dr. Diomampo/ Dr. Dy/ Dr. Moscoso
17. -- MRA ROTATOR'S NOTES -- Updated APs re: intra-operative findings and course Continue vital signs monitoring Kindly ff up post-op labs  Thank you!
18. NEURO May discontinue Mannitol.  BP target: 150-170mmHg Na target: 150-155 May augment BP: Norepinephrine (Norkenz) 8mg in 100cc PNSS to achieve BP target Dr. Liquete/ Bao-in
19. MROD: Continue totilac x 40cc/hr. # Hypokalemia (deficit 66) Give KCL side drip. 40meqs kcl in 100cc PNSS X 4meqs/hr for 1 more cycle.
20. MROD: continue to hold all antihypertensives. (Telmisartan, Carvedilol).

FINAL REMINDER: Output ONLY the summary paragraph. No extra text, no greetings, no bullet points. Do not mention or echo the reference examples.

Totilac was increased from 30 to 50 cc/hr then decreased to 40 cc/hr, the nicardipine drip was resumed at 1 mg/hr, serum sodium was monitored q8h, a KCl side drip 40 mEq in 100 cc PNSS at 4 mEq/hr was given for hypokalemia, and Zynapse 1 g IV q8h was started. Pre-operatively, the patient was kept on NPO with CBG q4h, 2 units pRBC were secured, blood typing, PT/PTT, and creatinine were requested, and risk stratification classified the patient as intermediate cardiac risk (5%) and high pulmonary risk (13.3%). The patient underwent left pterional craniotomy with clipping of the left posterior communicating artery aneurysm under GETA with scalp block and insertion of a lumbar drain. Post-operatively, the patient was reconnected to mechanical ventilation (AC mode, TV 380, BUR 16, I:E 1:2.5) with ABG after 30 minutes, the lumbar drain and NGT were maintained, and paracetamol 1 g IV q6 x 4 doses then 600 mg IV q6 RTC, ketorolac 30 mg IV q6 x 5 doses, fentanyl 50 mcg IV q4, ondansetron 4 mg IV q8 x 2 doses, ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD, and chlorhexidine gargle TID were given, with diazepam 5 mg IV on standby for seizures. Mannitol was discontinued and all antihypertensives were held to maintain SBP at 150-170 mmHg with norepinephrine 8 mg in 100 cc PNSS to augment BP if needed, serum sodium was targeted at 150-155, and post-operative CBC, electrolytes, iCa, Mg, and creatinine were requested.

CURRENT DOCTOR'S ORDERS:
1. MICU ROD: Diet: NPO, except oral meds via NGT  IVF/Drips: -PNSS 1L x 120cc/hr -Totilac 40cc/hr  Airway:    VAC:    FiO2: 60%     TV: 380    BUR: 16    I:E: 1:2.5    PEEP: 5  Diagnostics: -Serum Na Q8H -CBG Q6H while on NPO -2D echo result  # Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with Intraventricular Extension secondary to Ruptured Left Middle Cerebral Artery Aneurysm, Hypertension secondary, Acute respiratory failure type 1 secondary, s/p s/p Left pterional craniotomy, clipping of left posterior communicating artery aneurysm. -Totilac 40cc/hr -Nimodipine 30mg 2 tabs Q4H -Edaravone 30mg IV Q12H -PCT 600mg IV Q6 RTC -Levetiracetam 500mg 1 tab BID -Zynapse 1g IV Q8H  -Ketorolac 30mg IV Q8H PRN -Metoclopramide 10mg IV Q8H PRN -Omeprazole (Prosec) 40mg IV Q12H  -NAC 600mg 1 tab OD -Lactulose 20cc OD if no BM for the day -Standby Norepinephrine (Norkenz) 8mg in 100cc PNSS to target SBP 150-170mmHg. Serum Na: 150-155mmo/L Moderate High Back Rest, 30 degrees head at Midline  # Hypokalemia: - 40 meqs KCl + 100cc PNSS x 4 meqs/hr.  WOF worsening of neuro status, seizures, hypotension.
2. NSS May resume OF feeding NSS wise Refer accordingly  Dr. Diomampo/langeg
3. Anesthesia  Fully recovered from effects of anesthesia  Continue present management  Refer accordingly  Dr. LMA Domingo/Azuro
4. IM PULMO Shift the following setting to mech vent setting VSIMV TV 380 Fsimv 16 T insp 0.95 PEEP 5 Psupp 24  Dr Andal/Talampas/Paras/Sarmiento
5. MROD Increase Totilac to 60cc/hr ctalampas
6. maintain elastic bandage and lumbar drain replace lumbar drain drainage bag as needed continue meds
7. NEUROLOGY Decrease totilac to 50cc/hr Dr. Liquete/paras/Talampas
8. #Hazy urine output, r/o CAUTI For Urinalysis Please change IFC gently and aseptically ctalampas
9. NEURO NOTES Appraised relatives of patient’s current condition Focal deficits may be due to vasospasm Maintain SBP 150-170mmHg Continue medications Dr. Liquete/Talampas
10. MROD Increase Totilac to 60cc/hr ctalampas  NEURO Agree with plans Dr. Liquete/Talampas
11. MROD Please include serum K on the next lab extraction ctalampas

FINAL REMINDER: Output ONLY the summary paragraph. No extra text, no greetings, no bullet points. Do not mention or echo the reference examples.

Oral feeding via NGT was resumed, Totilac was titrated between 50 and 60 cc/hr, and mechanical ventilation was shifted to VSIMV (TV 380, rate 16, Tinsp 0.95, PEEP 5, PS 24). SBP was maintained at 150-170 mmHg with medications continued, the elastic bandage and lumbar drain were maintained with the drainage bag replaced as needed, and serum K was included in the next lab extraction. For hazy urine output, urinalysis was requested and the IFC was changed.

Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD – D3 (03/12) Totilac currently at 60cc/hr Nicardipine drip to maintain SBP of 150-170mmHg Nimodipine 30mg 2 tabs Q4H Edaravone 30mg IV Q12H Paracetamol 600mg IV Q6 RTC Levetiracetam 500mg/tab, 1 tab BID Zynapse 1g IV Q8H  Ketorolac 30mg IV Q8H PRN Metoclopramide 10mg IV Q8H PRN Omeprazole (Prosec) 40mg IV Q12H  NAC 600mg 1 tab OD Lactulose 20cc OD if no BM for the day Standby Diazepam 5mg IV for Frank Seizures (Max dose of 30 mg) ON HOLD: Telmisartan and Carvedilol  #Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection Ceftriaxone as above  TARGET PARAMETERS: [ ] SBP: 150-170mmHg. [ ] Serum Na: 150-155mmo/L [ ] Moderate High Back Rest, 30 degrees head at Midline  # Hypokalemia, correction done  ctalampas

8. Refer accordingly.

10. 12. NEUROLOGY For serial monitoring of weakness on the right side of the body Continue maintaining BP between 150-170mmHg Dr. Liquete/paras
13. PULMONOLOGY Shift MV settings VSIMV Fio2: 40% Vt: 380 Fsimv: 12 Tinsp: 1.25 PEEP: 5 Psupp 10 Continue titrating down psupp to 8 as tolerated Dr. Andal/paras/ULYA
14. MICU Increase totilac to 50cc/hr Please strictly maintain SBP of 130-170, adjust nicardipine drip accordingly paras.
15. MICU Resume telmisartan 40mg/tab 1 tab now paras.

17. MICU Follow-up repeat serum Na paras.
18. MICU  Increase totilac to 60cc/hr  paras.

FINAL REMINDER: Output ONLY the summary paragraph. No extra text, no greetings, no bullet points. Do not mention or echo the reference examples.

For catheter-associated UTI, urine GS/CS was sent and ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD was continued, IVF was decreased to 100 cc/hr, and CBG monitoring was changed to q4h pre-feeding. A KCl drip 40 mEq in 100 cc NSS at 4 mEq/hr x 3 cycles and KCl tablets 1 tab TID x 9 doses were started for hypokalemia, IV paracetamol was shifted to paracetamol 500 mg 1 tab q6 x 3 more days, and celecoxib 200 mg 1 cap BID x 4 days was started with fentanyl 50 mcg IV q4 PRN. Pressure support was titrated down by 2 every hour and the ventilator was shifted to VSIMV (FiO2 40%, TV 380, rate 12, Tinsp 1.25, PEEP 5, PS 10), and the lumbar drain bag was changed aseptically. Totilac was adjusted between 40 and 60 cc/hr, SBP was strictly maintained at 130-170 mmHg with the nicardipine drip titrated accordingly, telmisartan 40 mg 1 tab was resumed, right-sided weakness was serially monitored, and serum Na was repeated.
